Inside the village, the Co-op is a warm public room of tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, chipped mugs, and people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both. Run the Co-op as a social hub: shoe custom, regulars, games, tavern prompts, and trust-building. Mismatched chairs face inward, shoe lines mark the threshold, and gift shelves hold jars, cloth, ribbons, and careful generosity. Tea pours, mugs knock softly, someone clears their throat before hard news, and a ward chime outside lands a little flat. Clover honey, tea steam, wet boot leather, old wood warmed by bodies, and food stretched with pride instead of abundance. Counters are nicked smooth; mugs are chipped in familiar places; wool sleeves stay damp near the door. The room tracks manners. People...
